status: NOT FOR INSERT — failed nosource, elimination and withsource. Distractors only were rewritten; utterance, stem, key and difficulty are byte-identical to the live rows.

apparatus.note: Three independent Claude solvers per run. Validated by re-measuring the UNREPAIRED live cohort first: an attack that cannot reproduce the known-bad number cannot certify a repaired one.
apparatus.rejectedProtocol: per-item gpt-4.1 / gpt-4o / gpt-4.1-mini scored the unrepaired cohort at +8.0 against a recorded +65.7, so that protocol was discarded as unable to see the defect at all
apparatus.scorer: scripts/study-bank/score-blind.mjs reports PASS on an empty or truncated solver file and still applies the superseded mean<=control bar, so a strict wrapper was used for every number here

ceiling.basis: ETS Choose a Response published margin +25.5 plus the 4pt tolerance; ceilingFor() in src/lib/study/bank-ledger.ts

metrics.note: The same script FAILS the unrepaired cohort on five measures, including P(key | opener "yes") = 0%, P(key | opener "great") = 0%, P(key | two sentences) = 50%, and key structurally unique in 57.7% of items.
selfInflictedAndFixed: round 1 put the key at a length extreme in 64.8% of items (chance 50%)
round 1 opened 34 of 213 distractors with "I'll" against 3 of 71 keys — P(key) 8%
the fix for that created a "could" cluster — 17 distractors, 1 key, P(key) 5.6%
round 1 left P(key | two sentences) at 68%, named by a solver before any check saw it

metrics.ablationNote: Key plus three distractors from UNRELATED items scores 40.8% against a 31.0% control, with 1 of the solver’s 4 confident picks correct. The documented ablation on the unrepaired bank was 81.4% against 31.4%. The repaired keys no longer announce themselves in isolation; the residual signal is RELATIONAL — the three distractors let a solver reconstruct the withheld utterance and then pick the reply that fits it.

metrics.failingOption: Put me on it. So I am registered for the course from today, then? (delivered wording uses the contraction)
metrics.failingReason: conflates being waitlisted with being registered — self-contradictory whatever the utterance was
metrics.note: Round 1 passed this gate 0/71 on the same item. Round 2 split that option’s em-dash into a sentence break, which made the contradiction salient — so the round-1 pass on item 43 was borderline, not clean.

Difficulty moved the right way on every axis — hard 0% to 15.5%, multi-fact 7% to 45%, trivial 2 to 0 — so closeness was NOT bought with easiness. The blocker is the opposite failure: making distractors plausible without the source made 16 of them defensible WITH it.

knownDefects.detail: Self-contradictory distractor, named above. Left in the file rather than silently edited after the gates ran — hash binding exists to stop exactly that. Fix in round 3 with the ambiguous items and re-run every stage.
Date arithmetic wearing a pragmatics frame. Inherited: the utterance and key are original and out of scope for a distractor-only rewrite.
Near-duplicate scenarios (noise through a shared wall, hedged complaint). Inherited from the live bank.

nextRound: The 16 twoDefensible items cluster into three shapes: "Have you thought about X?" openers where accepting and counter-proposing are both natural; a stated obstacle where "work around it" and "ask for an alternative" are equally licensed; and complaint items where two different remedies both resolve it. Each needs the second-best option made wrong on a stated fact WITHOUT making it rejectable blind — which is the narrow corridor this pilot located and did not fully clear.
